version.changelog: Initial ClawHub release: Continuous self-improvement through structured reflection

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: self-reflection
Version: 1.1.1

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle 'self-reflection' is classified as benign. The skill's purpose is to enable continuous self-improvement for an AI agent by tracking mistakes and logging lessons. It integrates with OpenClaw's heartbeat mechanism, instructing the agent via `SKILL.md` to run local `self-reflection` commands (`check`, `read`, `log`) and store data in local markdown and JSON files (`~/workspace/memory/self-review.md`, `~/.openclaw/self-review-state.json`). There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection with a harmful objective. The required binaries (`jq`, `date`) are standard utilities, and the installation steps are typical for a CLI tool.

llm.summary: This self-reflection skill is understandable in purpose, but it asks users to run a recurring command from an unpinned external GitHub checkout and persist agent memory without enough safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The skill writes durable memory under ~/workspace/memory/self-review.md and state under ~/.openclaw/self-review-state.json; this fits the purpose but is broad enough to retain sensitive operational details if the agent logs them.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The README instructs users to git clone https://github.com/hopyky/self-reflection.git from a mutable branch and symlink its bin/self-reflection into ~/bin, so executable behavior can come from outside the reviewed artifact and change after review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The HEARTBEAT.md instructions make self-reflection check required on each heartbeat and tell the agent to read prior lessons and log insights on ALERT, without clear opt-in boundaries, exclusions, or controls for what task content may be written.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Cross-session memory and timer state are explicitly configured, and recurring heartbeat use makes the behavior persistent across tasks; the artifacts do not document retention, redaction, deletion, or secret-handling safeguards.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose of logging agent lessons is coherent, but the reviewed artifact does not include the documented bin/self-reflection executable while the skill instructions depend on that command for check, read, log, stats, and reset behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Only use it if you are comfortable with a recurring agent workflow that reads and writes local memory, and install the executable from a pinned, reviewed commit or release instead of a mutable GitHub branch. Configure the memory path deliberately, inspect it regularly, and do not let agents log secrets, credentials, private prompts, customer data, or sensitive incident details.
llm.findings:
[T03] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the README's unpinned git clone plus PATH symlink exposes a missing, externally fetched executable to recurring agent invocation.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted: persistent reflection memory is central to the skill, but the artifact lacks warnings against storing secrets, private user data, or sensitive incident/workflow details.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded from rogue-agent framing: state and memory files are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but still contribute to Review because they persist task-derived content without retention or sanitization controls.
[SQP-1] expected: Accepted as a scoping concern: heartbeat-triggered checks are part of the design, but the required automatic read/log flow is under-scoped for unrelated tasks and sensitive contexts.
